analysis:
Both changed files are offline CI routing test scripts: scripts/test-ci-component-paths.py and scripts/test-darkbloom-route.py. They do not touch provider runtime code, the coordinator-provider WebSocket, keys, attestation, App Attest authorization, cache storage or any other asset in the threat model.

The change removes the retained console lane. In test-ci-component-paths.py it drops console expectations: console-ui/package-lock.json, the .githooks entries, the protocol testdata fixtures and the lint-console job checks. It also drops the console-ui exemption from the forbidden-string check, so the public provider workflows are now asserted to contain no console-ui/ text at all. That tightens the check.

The security-relevant assertions are retained or strengthened. These include fork PRs never contacting the plane, certificate verification staying on, HTTPS-only plane URLs, exact label-array grants, read-only permissions with no id-token, and literal runners for release and credentialed workflows. The NUL-delimited filename test gains a new case, a docs file with a newline in its name that must not be split into a provider path.

In test-darkbloom-route.py the lint-console lane is replaced by a docs lane with count 0 in the fixture. The ROUTED entry for lint-console is removed, and the CONSOLE expression is removed from the file.

One minor coverage note is that console fixture-parity checks are removed. This reduces test coverage but is consistent with the console moving out of scope, and it is not a provider security control. I did not see the actual workflow YAML, scripts/ci-component-paths.py or the routing implementation. Whether those files drop the console lane consistently is outside the supplied evidence, but a mismatch would fail these tests rather than weaken security. No threat-model update is needed.
